decoder-transformer.name: decoder Transformer
decoder-transformer.definition: A stack of causal self-attention and position-wise feed-forward blocks used for autoregressive prediction.
decoder-transformer.explanation: A decoder maps token and position embeddings through repeated residual blocks, then projects final hidden states to next-token logits. In the chapter's pre-normalized form, each attention or feed-forward branch receives layer-normalized input and its output adds to an identity path. Causal masking prevents future-token access. Training must propagate cross-entropy gradients through the output head, final normalization, every reversed block, and both embedding tables. A complete decoder is an architecture; language quality still depends on data, optimization, scale, and evaluation.

residual-path.name: residual path
residual-path.definition: An identity connection that adds a block input to a learned update of the same shape.
residual-path.explanation: For y=x+f(x), forward preserves x while adding a learned change. Backward sends the upstream gradient directly to x and also through f, then sums both contributions. Residual paths help information and gradients traverse deep stacks, but they require matching shapes. In a decoder block, attention and feed-forward branches each have their own residual addition. Forgetting the direct gradient can leave earlier parameters with weak or zero updates even when the output head learns.

layer-normalization.name: layer normalization
layer-normalization.definition: Per-token feature normalization followed by learned gain and bias.
layer-normalization.explanation: Layer normalization computes mean and variance across a hidden row's features, independently for each token. It centers and scales the row, then applies trainable vectors γ and β. Unlike batch normalization, it uses the same type of statistics during training and inference and does not mix examples. Backward must include the dependence of mean and variance on every feature. The chapter uses pre-normalization, so normalized values enter each learned branch while the residual identity remains unnormalized.

gelu.name: Gaussian error linear unit
gelu.definition: A smooth activation that gates a scalar according to its magnitude.
gelu.explanation: GELU multiplies an input by a smooth approximation to the probability that a related Gaussian variable falls below it. Transformer feed-forward blocks commonly use it between their expansion and contraction projections. This chapter implements the tanh approximation and differentiates that exact formula during backward. Matching the derivative to the forward approximation matters for gradient checks. Unlike ReLU, negative inputs can retain small nonzero outputs and gradients rather than being cut off abruptly.
